children: has won offshore facilities work orders worth MYR475mn (about $115.4mn) from PETRONAS Carigali, the exploration unit wholly owned by Malaysia's state energy company Petroliam Nasional (PETRONAS),
reports. The work orders fall under an existing contract for transporting and installing offshore facilities.

The award adds to the domestic pipeline of the oilfield services group, formerly known as Sapura Energy. The company returned to profit in its most recent reported quarter after completing a restructuring exercise. As of July 31, it had an order book of MYR7bn, plus a further MYR2.7bn attributable to joint ventures and associates.

Its subsidiary, VTEB Offshore, accepted the orders on August 5 and October 6, according to a stock exchange filing. Work started in the quarter that ended on October 31 and should be finished by the fourth quarter of the financial year ending January 31, 2028. PETRONAS Carigali may choose to exercise optional scopes included in one of the orders.

Group Chief Operating Officer Louay Laham said the contract came from the company's decision to concentrate on markets and capabilities where it holds a competitive edge. He described Malaysia as a core market and said transportation and installation remained an area offering attractive opportunities.

Vantris Energy has not yet released results for the quarter ended October 31. In the previous quarter, it posted a net profit of MYR75.3mn, against a net loss of MYR230.8mn a year before. Smaller foreign exchange losses and lower finance costs after the restructuring drove the turnaround.

Revenue for that quarter dropped 23% to MYR818.5mn from MYR1.06bn. Weaker contributions from engineering and construction, as projects ended and ongoing jobs advanced more slowly, weighed on the figure.

On November 18, Vantris Energy and Paratus Energy Services, its equal partner in the Brazilian subsea venture Seagems Solutions, said they were considering selling the business after a review. A day earlier, Seagems had secured a $410mn contract from Petrobras for subsea engineering and installation services.
Vantris Energy shares fell half a sen, or 2%, to MYR24.5 cents on November 25, giving the company a market value of MYR567.6mn.

title: Malaysia's Vantris Energy wins $115.4mn Petronas offshore contract
